diffs.diff: header pin 1: part says GND, datasheet reading says CH1+
diffs.evidence: Same board, two different pin-numbering conventions; no signal is actually on a different physical pin. DFRobot DFR0316 silkscreen/pinout image (what the user sees) reads, top to bottom: left header GND, +5V, C3+, C3-, C4+, C4-; right header SCL, SDA, C2-, C2+, C1-, C1+ -- exactly the model's pins 1-12. The DFR0316 schematic numbers the headers the other way: P1 pin1..6 = CH1+, CH1-, CH2+, CH2-, SDAr, SCLr and P2 pin1..6 = CH4-, CH4+, CH3-, CH3+, +5V, GND, which is the second reading's order. Reversing each schematic header gives P2 6..1 = GND, +5V, CH3+, CH3-, CH4+, CH4- and P1 6..1 = SCL, SDA, CH2-, CH2+, CH1-, CH1+, identical to the model (same neighbours: e.g. +5V sits between GND and CH3+ in both). The second reading simply lists the schematic's connector pin 1 first and P1 before P2. For this line: header pin 1 is the same physical pad in both readings once the header numbering direction is accounted for; the model follows the board silkscreen order.
